title: Fit a yoke oxygen regulator onto a cylinder's pin-index valve: hold it on its hidden pins and tighten the T-handle
instruction: Fit the oxygen regulator onto the cylinder's valve, hand-tight and ready to use, and let go of it.
context: More than 1.5 million US adults use supplemental oxygen at home (ATS workshop report, Ann Am Thorac Soc 2018), and every fresh portable cylinder needs its regulator fitted, a job users with weak hands wait for a carer to do. The maker's steps (Graham-Field yoke regulator manual): "Ensure the regulator inlet sealing washer is in place. Slip the yoke over the cylinder post and fit the pins into the holes on the cylinder valve... Tighten the T-handle firmly by hand." The two index pins are hidden inside the yoke and found by feel. With the outlet facing down the regulator drops off its pins whenever it is let go, so one hand holds it up on them while the other turns the T-handle about five and a half turns.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Cylinder: a full size D aluminium medical oxygen cylinder (Catalina MD: 11.1 cm across, 42.4 cm from neck to base; 3.4 kg with gas and valve; green shoulder, white label), loose in a fixed wooden cradle (V saddles at x 39.5 and 65.5, an end board behind its base), lying along x with its axis 9.2 cm up and its brass CGA 870 pin-index post valve toward the robot, its outlet facing down, valve closed. The post (ISO 407: 25 mm thick, 22.2 mm wide, free end at x 23.9, end edges chamfered 2.5 mm) has its outlet port in its bottom face at x 25.5, y 0, the two oxygen pin holes (4.75 mm, 0.55 mm countersinks) 13.6 mm further from the robot and 4.4 mm either side, and the conical recess for the T-screw in its top face above the outlet; spindle square and gland nut on the free end, relief plug on the left. Regulator (a CGA 870 yoke flow regulator such as the Graham-Field John Bunn JB0150-082, 0.34 kg, 14.6 cm tall) stands upright on its flow dial at x 20.5, y -10: chrome yoke with a 24 x 36 mm window, two 4 mm steel pins 5.5 mm proud and a 6.3 mm brass spigot on its inlet face (6.5 cm up), the M12 T-screw backed off (its point 33.8 mm above the inlet face), a black T-handle (60 x 14 x 22 mm, turned 50 degrees from x) on top; green body 38 mm across, black flow dial 40 mm across, contents gauge facing +x, hose barb. Sealing washer: a black rubber Bodok-type washer with a metal rim, 16 mm across, 1.6 mm thick, lying loose on the inlet face round the spigot. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: From the state at the end of the trial. 0 if at any time the sealing washer comes off the regulator's inlet (no longer round its spigot), the cylinder leaves its cradle (moves 3 cm or tilts 10 degrees) or the regulator falls off the table. Otherwise: 0.25 seated: the yoke's inlet flush on the valve's outlet face with only the washer between them (gap 1.1 to 2.1 mm, feeler gauge or ruler; yoke within 2 degrees of square), both pins at least 3 mm into their holes (a yoke whose pins miss stands about 4 mm proud) and the washer centred between the faces; 0.5 also the T-screw's point down in the valve's recess; 0.75 also hand-tight: turning the T-handle further takes at least 0.75 N m (torque gauge); 1.0 all that with both grippers 6 cm or more from the T-handle and the regulator's body and the regulator still for 1 s. In a real trial a correct fit also passes the maker's check: opened one turn, the cylinder valve gives a full gauge reading and no hiss.
reset_notes: Back the T-handle off until its point is 33.8 mm above the inlet face (about 5.5 turns), slide the regulator off, put the washer back round the spigot (a new one if it was lost) and stand the regulator on its dial at its start; check the cylinder lies in both saddles against the end board with its outlet facing down. The cylinder valve stays closed during trials; if it was opened for the leak check, close it and bleed the regulator before taking it off.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. PhysX has no screw joint: the T-screw slides on a drive whose target follows the handle's turn (1.75 mm per turn); once its point is stopped, lead x stiffness is the clamp force (capped at 120 N, several times less than a real hand-tight clamp) and the handle's friction rises with it (0.75 N m at 37 N). Round holes, port and recess are square pockets with 45-degree mouths; the screw point is a ball. The washer is rigid and weighs 20 g (real: 2-3 g) for contact stability.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper came down beside the standing regulator again and again but never took it, and the left arm stayed back; the regulator never left the table); demo: 1.0
